title: Projects
text:
Hackathons

2015 · Safer Baltimore Biking, JHU Data Science Hackathon. Used open Baltimore City data on accidents and road hazards to map road safety; geocoded hazards and helped build the final Leaflet map.
2015 · IdEar, MedHacks 1.0. A proof of concept that ears can act as biometric markers where population registries are poor, using SIFT features and an SVM. Top 10 of 30 teams.

title: John Muschelli
text:
My name is John Muschelli (pronounced Moo-shell-e), and I am an Associate Research Professor in the Department of Biostatistics at the Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health (JHSPH). I received my ScM in Biostatistics under the advising of Brian Caffo and my PhD under Ciprian Crainiceanu, both from JHSPH, and a BS in Biomathematics and Neuroscience from the University of Scranton.
I work on wearable and accelerometry data (step counts, sleep, physical activity in studies like NHANES and UK Biobank) and on processing and analyzing medical images, usually of the brain. I write a lot of R software to make that easier, teach data science, and co-host the podcast The Corresponding Author.
My blog, A HopStat and a Jump Away, is updated much more often than this site.
